items.title: SpaceX catches upper stage of Starship rocket in historic first
items.english: SpaceX catches upper stage of Starship rocket in historic first
items.summary: SpaceX successfully caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket from orbit using mechanical arms at its Starbase facility in Texas during Test Flight 15. The milestone follows a booster explosion earlier in the test, which prevented the recovery of the first-stage booster. Making Starship fully reusable is critical for SpaceX to launch more Starlink satellites and support future lunar and Martian missions.

items.title: ChatGPT Wallet
items.english: ChatGPT Wallet
items.summary: OpenAI is introducing ChatGPT Wallet, a payment feature that allows AI agents to make secure purchases on behalf of users without exposing actual card details. Built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa, the feature requires user approval and a security check for every transaction while preserving existing card rewards and dispute protections. The wallet is rolling out initially to US ChatGPT Pro subscribers through dots.

items.title: NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition
items.english: NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition
items.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned as President, CEO, and board member of NVIDIA, effective immediately. Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and CFO, has been appointed interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. Additionally, Harvey C. Jones has been appointed as the first-ever Chair of the Board.

items.title: How Jensen Huang Built the Backdoor Route That Keeps Beijing in the AI Race
items.english: How Jensen Huang Built the Backdoor Route That Keeps Beijing in the AI Race
items.summary: Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang was ousted following the development of a massive data-center hub in Malaysia designed to supply advanced American artificial-intelligence chips to Chinese customers. Industry leaders note that the site and others like it allow Chinese companies to access top-tier hardware outside Washington's reach. Huang reportedly cultivated Asian partners and lobbied Washington to keep this backdoor route open for Chinese buyers.

items.title: Top Chinese Frontier AI Models Carry the Fingerprint of Export-Controlled NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs · Unemployment Labs
items.english: Top Chinese Frontier AI Models Carry the Fingerprint of Export-Controlled NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs · Unemployment Labs
items.summary: A forensic analysis of publicly released AI model weights indicates that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group have gained access to export-controlled NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs to create their latest models. By examining numerical patterns and thread counts matching Blackwell hardware initialization, researchers identified six models released between April and November 2026 that carry these hardware fingerprints, contrasting with earlier models trained on Hopper-generation chips.

items.title: Samsung Intelligent Eyewear Android XR launches mid-December
items.english: Samsung Intelligent Eyewear Android XR launches mid-December
items.summary: Google has announced pre-orders for new Intelligent Eyewear collections developed in collaboration with Gentle Monster, Warby Parker, and Samsung. Powered by Gemini, the frames offer real-time assistance, turn-by-turn directions, translation, and hands-free media controls, alongside a 12-megapixel camera and robust privacy protections. The glasses are priced starting at $395 and will be available in stores and online beginning December 10.

items.title: End‑to‑End 4‑Bit Training - Thinking Machines Lab
items.english: End‑to‑End 4‑Bit Training - Thinking Machines Lab
items.summary: Thinking Machines Lab details its end-to-end 4-bit training methodology for large language models using NVIDIA's GB300 platform and NVFP4 precision. By combining forward-pass NVFP4 quantization with stochastic rounding for backward passes, random Hadamard transforms for communication bottlenecks, and custom fused kernels, the team achieved an 8 percent pretraining speedup and a 20 percent reinforcement learning speedup on Inkling 2 Small.

items.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen
items.english: Introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen
items.summary: Google has introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a new model designed for rapid execution in coding and agentic workflows, rolling out globally across developer, enterprise, and consumer surfaces. Hydrogen offers four thinking levels, a 1 million-token context window, and improved speed, accuracy, and safety compared to its predecessor. Additionally, Google launched the Orchestrator tool in Google Antigravity to dynamically switch between Gemini models in multi-model workflows.

items.title: Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
items.english: Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
items.summary: A petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate ousted CEO Jensen Huang has attracted more than 115,000 signatures, including high-profile tech executives such as Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney. The signers argue that Huang was removed without meaningful due process following reports regarding his extramarital affairs and relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Meanwhile, Nvidia appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO while its stock fell following the departure.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s exit puts Nvidia’s support for open source in question
items.english: Jensen Huang’s exit puts Nvidia’s support for open source in question
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned following an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, casting uncertainty over the company's commitment to the open-source AI community and ongoing deals such as the acquisition of Hugging Face. Huang was a leading advocate for open-source AI and pushed back against U.S. restrictions on open-weight models, making his departure a potential turning point for Nvidia's strategy and Washington policy debates. CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as questions mount regarding the future of Nvidia's open-source initiatives.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra helps define Standard Model on lattice
items.english: GPT-6 Astra helps define Standard Model on lattice
items.summary: Physicist Nathaniel Craig and GPT-6 Astra have developed a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition for the Standard Model of particle physics, addressing a fifty-year-old challenge involving chiral theories and quantum phase corrections. The approach uses finer grids to compute and compensate for the phase shifts of left-handed fermions. While this provides an answer in principle, further expert dialogue and work are required to make the construction practical for realistic simulations.

items.title: Vulcan rocket fails during launch, dealing major blow to SpaceX competitors
items.english: Vulcan rocket fails during launch, dealing major blow to SpaceX competitors
items.summary: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket suffered a total mission failure ten minutes after liftoff from Cape Canaveral, destroying 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites. The incident marks the first total mission failure for ULA since its formation and is expected to ground the rocket indefinitely, dealing a major blow to Amazon and the US Space Force.

items.title: Stanford AI Index finds AI investment tops $1 trillion
items.english: Stanford AI Index finds AI investment tops $1 trillion
items.summary: New findings from the Stanford AI Index reveal that global corporate investment in artificial intelligence has surpassed $1 trillion in 2026. However, public sentiment and labor market outcomes show an uneven picture, with more people globally expecting AI to eliminate jobs than create them and employment declines deepening among younger and AI-exposed workers.

items.title: AI agents need isolated sandboxes for PR validation
items.english: AI agents need isolated sandboxes for PR validation
items.summary: The author argues that AI agents require isolated sandboxes to safely test and validate their code changes before submitting pull requests. Various sandbox designs—ranging from lightweight faked islands and local dev setups to ephemeral containers and preview environments—offer different trade-offs between realism, safety, and speed. To make these sandboxes effective, teams must provide proper isolation, daily test-data snapshots, dev-only logins, and execution receipts.

items.title: Ashfurrow argues for agentic coding trust framework
items.english: Ashfurrow argues for agentic coding trust framework
items.summary: The author argues that adopting agentic coding tools requires developers to change their mindset, embrace curiosity, and move through a trust ladder from line-by-line micromanagement to eventually trusting agents with merged pull requests. To safely utilize these non-deterministic tools, engineering teams must invest in robust software verifiability, automated testing, and strict guardrails to shift the development bottleneck from code generation to code verification.

items.title: Blackwell to Rubin boosts low-latency inference capacity
items.english: Blackwell to Rubin boosts low-latency inference capacity
items.summary: The author analyzes how modern hardware improvements—from Blackwell to Rubin and beyond—disproportionately boost AI inference performance at the interactivity level compared to basic concurrency metrics. By modeling a 3-trillion-parameter extrapolation of Llama 3, the analysis shows that faster chips shrink the fixed cost of every decode step, significantly increasing the user capacity under low-latency targets. However, due to ongoing hardware supply constraints, the industry will likely continue running inference on older hardware to meet infinite demand for tokens.

items.title: M-Vave FM-1 publishes GPLv3 firmware and kit
items.english: M-Vave FM-1 publishes GPLv3 firmware and kit
items.summary: The author argues that as AI coding tools make writing and replacing device firmware increasingly cheap and fast, consumer electronics that allow custom software modifications will become more popular. The author predicts that consumer AI agents will soon handle installing or writing custom firmware to fix issues, leading buyers to favor hackable hardware and pressuring manufacturers to open their platforms.

items.title: How Jensen Huang’s exit from Nvidia impacts China’s AI supply chain
items.english: How Jensen Huang’s exit from Nvidia impacts China’s AI supply chain
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned following admissions of an affair with a Chinese data center executive linked to U.S. intelligence concerns. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been appointed interim CEO as the leadership transition creates uncertainty across Nvidia's supply chain and raises concerns about China's access to advanced AI chips.

items.title: Microlink cuts Kubernetes cold image pulls using zstd
items.english: Microlink cuts Kubernetes cold image pulls using zstd
items.summary: The authors explain how they reduced their Kubernetes image pull time from 111 seconds to 25 seconds for cold nodes. They achieved this by switching to zstd image compression using buildx, streamlining their base image and eliminating duplicate layers by consolidating build steps, and removing unnecessary files from node_modules. Additionally, they adjusted autoscaler settings and added a secondary node pool to mitigate capacity shortages.

items.title: Tesla opens Cybercab pre-orders ‘for personal use,’ with geo restrictions and a $299 monthly fee
items.english: Tesla opens Cybercab pre-orders ‘for personal use,’ with geo restrictions and a $299 monthly fee
items.summary: Tesla has opened pre-orders for its autonomous Cybercab for personal use to select customers in a handful of Texas cities, with deliveries estimated for December 2026. Buyers face a $29,990 price tag and a $299 monthly fee to operate the vehicle within geofenced areas. CEO Elon Musk stated that the vehicle will become available nationwide as regulatory approvals are received and noted that the monthly fee should eventually match the cost of other models at around $115 per month.
